skill.name: check-plan
skill.description: Audit implementation progress against a plan, verify completed work, identify remaining tasks, and validate quality for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
skill.summary: Check a plan against implementation work and produce a clear progress audit.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks around paths, examples, and code fences. The real risks are legitimate external-command instructions for git, grep, ls, gh, and package validation scripts. No prompt injection or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Package validation scripts may execute repository-defined code.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before npm scripts and prefer direct read-only commands when possible.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI lookup may use network access and local credentials.
remediation.suggestion: State that gh commands can contact GitHub and require consent in private repositories.
Label shell commands as optional validation steps and explain their expected scope.

content.value_statement: Implementation plans often drift from the actual code. This skill compares the plan, changed files, validation results, and remaining work so users can close gaps.
actual_capabilities: Reads a plan and maps each planned item to affected files.
Uses git status, diffs, and file searches to inspect implementation scope.
Checks removal requirements and flags old code that remains.
Compares original issue requirements with delivered implementation.
Runs or requests validation checks such as typecheck, lint, and build.
Produces a progress report with completed, partial, and remaining tasks.
limitations: It depends on access to the plan, repository, and issue context.
Validation commands may fail when project dependencies are missing.
It cannot prove runtime behavior without appropriate tests or builds.
It should not mark work complete when requirements are unclear.

use_cases.title: Pre-review plan audit
use_cases.description: Check whether a feature branch matches the approved implementation plan before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Release readiness check
use_cases.description: Verify plan completion, validation status, and unresolved gaps before a release milestone.

use_cases.title: Handoff cleanup
use_cases.description: Create a clear remaining-work list when ownership moves between contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Check my plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic progress review for one plan file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use check-plan to review the current branch against `.plans/my-feature.todo.md`. Tell me what is done and what remains.

prompt_templates.title: Verify removals
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused audit for deleted code and deprecated references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the removal spec in `.plans/refactor.todo.md`. Confirm old code is gone and list anything still present.

prompt_templates.title: Audit issue coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare original requirements with the plan and implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether issue 142 is fully covered by the plan and implementation. Flag missing requirements before final review.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare readiness report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with validation and prioritized next steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full check-plan audit for the active branch. Include validation status, quality issues, scope changes, and prioritized remaining tasks.

output_examples.output: Overall completion is 70 percent. Two plan steps are complete, one is partial, and removal work remains high priority.

output_examples.input: Verify the removal spec before I mark this plan done.
output: Completed removals: legacy helper import and old route file.
Pending removals: deprecated token function still appears in one service file.
Next step: remove the remaining reference and rerun validation.

output_examples.input: Audit whether the original issue is fully covered.
output_examples.output: The implementation covers the main workflow but misses one acceptance criterion for error handling. The plan should stay open.

best_practices: Provide the exact plan file and branch context before starting the audit.
Review command output carefully before marking validation as passed.
Keep remaining tasks specific enough for another contributor to complete.
anti_patterns: Do not mark a plan complete when original issue requirements are missing.
Do not skip files because they seem unrelated without checking the plan.
Do not run package scripts in untrusted repositories without user confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It compares a plan, changed files, removal requirements, quality checks, and validation results.

faq.question: Can it finish the implementation for me?
faq.answer: No. It audits progress and lists remaining work. It is not an implementation skill.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: It may run git, search, typecheck, lint, or build commands when the repository context allows them.

faq.question: Is it useful without a plan file?
faq.answer: It works best with a plan file. Without one, it needs a clear task or issue description.

faq.question: How does it handle partial work?
faq.answer: It separates completed, partial, and missing items, then prioritizes the next tasks.

faq.question: Can it validate original issue coverage?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares issue requirements with both the plan and the current implementation.
